clue.text: Bandaged by feathers and straw, that man in good health

indicators.note: something bandaged is wrapped round, so the pronoun is held inside the word for straw

parts.note: thatch is straw used for roofing

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from injury, bandaged up and lying on feathers and straw, is nonetheless pronounced fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good health' reads as a state of wellbeing, but it is the toast people say as they raise a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said before drinking, raised to wish others well.

clue.text: Brought into disrepute, fed up getting made wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
made wrong means put together incorrectly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone fed up after being falsely discredited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like the idiom for annoyed, but it is fed written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame someone is to damage their reputation, bringing them into disrepute.

clue.text: Big effort, one going on foot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for force
second meaning: a rubber boot, short for wellington

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give it some welly' is British slang for putting real effort in; a welly is also a wellington boot, a rubber rain boot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for vigour and an everyday British word for a waterproof boot worn on the foot.

clue.text: Small vehicle in row with estate after crashing

indicators.note: after a crash things are wrecked and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small car in an argument with an estate car after a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British name for a station wagon, which feeds the motoring scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater is a compact car or plane carrying just two people, a kind of small vehicle.

clue.text: Correct current passed up

indicators.note: in a down clue, passing up means travelling bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges they rightly let the flow go by.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and revise it.

clue.text: Eminent American ruler of empire

explanation.surface: A distinguished American heading an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, an example of an imperial ruler.

clue.text: Officer doubling up on a drink

explanation.surface: An officer doubles up over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the doubled officer sits on top of the a.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink.

clue.text: Chilli, for example, flavour of the month?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something spicy, literally hot
second meaning: someone or something currently very popular

explanation.walkthrough: Flavour sounds culinary like chilli, but the phrase means the latest fashionable thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy food is literally hot, and a person in great demand is informally called hot property.

clue.text: Part of chest, one drawer out of it

indicators.note: part of means only a portion of the following run of letters is used

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture: part of a chest, with one drawer taken out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of it' looks like the drawer being removed, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of it is slang for intoxicated by drink or drugs.

clue.text: Fluid including oil drained next

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: fluid as in smooth and running

indicators.note: a drained word has had its contents emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A liquid with drained oil in it sounds like a car mechanic's notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Following and next are synonyms for what comes immediately after.

clue.text: Power punch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: influence, as in political weight

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a boxer's big hit, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means influence or leverage, and is also an informal word for a hard blow.

clue.text: Traditional UK general election time bound to be chaos

parts.note: British general elections have customarily been held in May
a hem is a border or boundary, so to hem is to bound

explanation.surface: A political commentator predicts the usual election season will end in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Many UK general elections fell in May, which makes it the conventional election month.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or confusion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Hired gun: twin fools in for it?

parts.note: two asses, an ass being a fool

explanation.surface: Two idiots who hired a gunman are now in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In for it' suggests trouble, but here 'in' is simply taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired gun is a paid killer, which is what an assassin is.

clue.text: Cut ends off old sausage roll, the worst piece

indicators.note: the ends taken off the following words are their final letters, which are kept

parts.words: old sausage roll, the worst piece
parts.note: the last letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone trims the ends from a stale sausage roll, the poorest bit of the buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut text is to remove it, the editing sense of the word.

clue.text: Tough knots lay there

indicators.note: knots tangle things, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Hard knots lay there in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or skin that is leathery is hard to chew or tear, so tough.

clue.text: Wrap up certain short series

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a round is a series, as of talks or drinks

explanation.surface: A TV commissioner decides to wrap up a brief run of episodes.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround something is to enclose it, the same as wrapping it up.

clue.text: American flower in Rhode Island, giant swallows also

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so the giant holds the next word

parts.note: an ogre is a giant of folklore

explanation.surface: An American flower growing in Rhode Island is eaten by a giant too.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river; the Rio Grande forms much of the US border with Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river, and the Rio Grande is a major North American river.

clue.text: Creator of new design put hole in wrought iron

indicators.note: the word in, after put, means one piece is set inside the other
wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A designer drills a hole in a piece of wrought iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrought iron' reads as the metal, but wrought is the instruction to rearrange iron.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor devises new machines or processes, creating original designs.

clue.text: Blatant placing of elderly relative in annexe?

indicators.note: placing something in another thing puts it inside, so the relative goes within

parts.note: a granny flat is an annexe, so the question mark hints at a flat

explanation.surface: Putting your old relative in an annexe looks like obvious neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny flat is a self-contained annexe for an elderly relative, hence the wry question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant and blatant both describe conduct that is shockingly obvious.

clue.text: Loud, like lightning?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gaudy and showy, as with clothes
second meaning: playfully, full of flashes

explanation.walkthrough: Loud suggests thunder alongside lightning, but it means garish; the question mark marks the jokey second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothes are showy and garish, and lightning comes in flashes, so is jokingly flashy.

clue.text: Party great for gossip

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous, great

explanation.surface: A party is great for catching up on the latest gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal chat, the same as a gossip.

clue.text: Bad leg I gathered, who cares?

indicators.note: gathered means collected up together in a heap, so the letters are bundled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a bad leg: so what?
explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically, 'big deal' is a dismissive retort meaning it doesn't matter.

clue.text: Hero getting cold in water, on the retreat

indicators.note: in places the word for cold inside the other piece
retreating means going back, so the word for water is read backwards

explanation.surface: A soldier retreating through cold water is called a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the greatest Greek warrior of the Trojan War, a hero of myth.

clue.text: Virtuoso with record on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: to list is to record in writing

explanation.surface: A great performer with a recording played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated 19th-century piano virtuoso and composer.

clue.text: Tiresome court procedure

definitions.meaning: second meaning: hearing a case before a judge

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a complaint about slow legal process; the second definition is a verb form, the act of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying describes something exhausting, and a court is trying a defendant when it hears the case.

clue.text: More slippery, every other bit of pitch, I hear

indicators.note: every other bit means taking one letter, skipping one, and so on

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator remarks that the pitch is getting more slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but its letters are simply part of the run being thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier surfaces are more covered in ice and so more slippery.

clue.text: Huge number of limbs, arguably?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a host or multitude
second meaning: playfully, the adjective from arm, like sandy from sand

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'arguably' flag an invented adjective: arm plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An army of people is a vast crowd, and an invented adjective for full of arms would be the same word.

clue.text: County pack members overheard?

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: hearts are one suit of cards in a pack

explanation.surface: Members of a wolf pack can be heard somewhere in a rural county.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent HEARTS and Herts sound alike; Herts is the short name for Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Herts is the standard abbreviation for Hertfordshire, an English shire.

clue.text: Bully sees girl is pinioned by rubber ring

indicators.note: someone pinioned is held tightly, so these words are gripped inside the ring

parts.note: a tyre is a ring of rubber

explanation.surface: A bully spots a girl stuck in a rubber swimming ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully is to tyrannise, dominating others cruelly.

clue.text: Bird demolished pretty morsel

indicators.note: something demolished is broken up, so the letters are knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A bird gobbled up a pretty little titbit.
explanation.definitionFit: The storm petrel is a small seabird, an example of the general class.
